core_obligations: Maps (proof lines 3556-3570): for a map of sheaves of sets the author shows that injectivity or surjectivity on all stalks at geometric points is equivalent to the corresponding property of the map, using the description of sections by coverings and the definition of the stalk.
Sequences (proof lines 3570-3580): for abelian sheaves the same argument applied to the maps in the sequence shows that exactness is equivalent to exactness of the induced sequences of stalks.
proof_roadmap: Test injectivity and surjectivity of a map on stalks.
Apply the criterion to each map in a sequence to conclude exactness.
difficulty_reason: The theorem shows that a map of sheaves of sets is injective or surjective exactly when its induced maps on stalks at geometric points are, and that a sequence of abelian sheaves is exact exactly when it is exact on all stalks (statement lines 3545-3554). The proof reduces both assertions to the description of sections of a sheaf by the members of a covering and the definition of the stalk (proof lines 3556-3580), the sequence statement following by applying the map statement to each map in the sequence. The non-formal content is the use of the stalk definition to promote stalkwise information to information on sections. The claim is H2: one argument applied twice.
